query: Tim Burton film where Johnny Depp plays an unfinished artificial man with scissors for hands, taken in by an Avon lady in a pastel suburb; he sculpts hedges and ice and falls for Winona Ryder's Kim. Vincent Price is his inventor.
Patrick Swayze is murdered and stays on as a ghost to protect Demi Moore, warning her through a fake psychic played by Whoopi Goldberg; the pottery wheel scene to 'Unchained Melody'.
Kevin Costner directs and stars as a Union lieutenant posted to an abandoned frontier fort who befriends a Lakota Sioux tribe and a wolf and gets a Sioux name. It won best picture I think.

Arnold Schwarzenegger as a construction worker who buys implanted memories of a trip to Mars and finds out his whole life is fake; the three-breasted woman and the mutants. Not the Colin Farrell remake.
Richard Gere as a rich corporate raider who hires Julia Roberts, a Hollywood Boulevard prostitute, to stay with him for a week, and they fall in love; the shopping scene on Rodeo Drive.

Disney animated musical where Belle takes her father's place as prisoner of a cursed Beast in a castle with a talking candlestick and teapot, and Gaston is the villain. The 1991 cartoon, not the Emma Watson remake.
Geena Davis and Susan Sarandon go on a road trip that turns into a run from the police after one shoots a man attacking the other; Brad Pitt is a hitchhiker, and they drive off into the Grand Canyon.

Tarantino's first film: jewel thieves with colour code names like Mr. White, Mr. Orange and Mr. Pink regroup in a warehouse after a heist goes wrong and one of them is an undercover cop; the ear scene to 'Stuck in the Middle with You'.

Disney cartoon with Robin Williams as the Genie of the lamp, a street rat who becomes Prince Ali to marry Princess Jasmine, and the villain Jafar with his parrot Iago. Not the Will Smith live action version.
Clint Eastwood as a retired gunfighter turned pig farmer who takes one last bounty job against cowboys who cut up a prostitute, with Morgan Freeman, against Gene Hackman's sheriff Little Bill.
Robin Williams dresses up as an old Scottish nanny to spend time with his kids after the divorce; Sally Field is the ex-wife and Pierce Brosnan the new boyfriend.
Harrison Ford as Dr. Richard Kimble, wrongly convicted of killing his wife, escapes when a train hits the prison bus and hunts the one-armed man while Tommy Lee Jones's US marshal chases him.
Keanu Reeves as a SWAT cop on a Los Angeles bus rigged to explode if it drops below 50 miles per hour; Sandra Bullock ends up driving and Dennis Hopper is the bomber. Early 2000s I think.
Jean Reno as a lonely hitman in New York who takes in 12-year-old Natalie Portman after a corrupt DEA agent played by Gary Oldman kills her family; he looks after a house plant. Luc Besson.
Jim Carrey as a shy bank clerk who finds a wooden mask that turns him into a green-faced cartoonish trickster; Cameron Diaz and the dog Milo. The original, not Son of the Mask.
Michael Mann crime film: Al Pacino as an LA detective chasing Robert De Niro's crew of professional thieves; the diner scene with both of them and the huge downtown shootout after the bank robbery.
Five criminals meet in a police line-up; Kevin Spacey's limping conman Verbal Kint tells a customs agent about the legendary Keyser Söze, and the twist at the end. Bryan Singer.
Tom Hanks, Kevin Bacon and Bill Paxton as astronauts whose moon mission fails after an oxygen tank explodes, 'Houston, we have a problem', and Ed Harris runs mission control to bring them home.
Scorsese mob epic: Robert De Niro runs a Las Vegas casino for the mafia, Joe Pesci is his violent friend and Sharon Stone the hustler wife. Not Goodfellas, the Vegas one.

Robin Williams comes out of a magic jungle board game after 26 years when two kids roll the dice, and every turn releases stampedes, monkeys and a hunter. The original with Kirsten Dunst, not the Dwayne Johnson one.
Bruce Willis is sent back in time from a plague-ravaged future to find the source of the virus and ends up in a mental hospital with Brad Pitt; Terry Gilliam.
Alien saucers blow up the White House; Will Smith as a fighter pilot and Jeff Goldblum as a computer expert upload a virus to the mothership, and the president gives a speech on the Fourth of July.
Coen brothers: a car salesman in Minnesota hires two crooks to kidnap his own wife, and a pregnant police chief, Marge Gunderson (Frances McDormand), investigates; the woodchipper.
Tom Cruise as a sports agent fired after writing a mission statement, left with one client, Cuba Gooding Jr.'s football player ('Show me the money!'); Renée Zellweger: 'you had me at hello'.
Will Smith and Tommy Lee Jones as secret agents in black suits who police aliens living on Earth and wipe people's memories with a flashing pen; a giant bug is the villain. The first one.
1950s Los Angeles police corruption: Guy Pearce, Russell Crowe and Kevin Spacey investigate the Nite Owl coffee shop massacre; Kim Basinger plays a call girl made up to look like Veronica Lake.
Jeff Bridges as the Dude, a lazy bowler in LA mistaken for a millionaire with the same name after thugs pee on his rug; John Goodman as Walter. Coen brothers.
Bruce Willis leads a team of oil drillers sent to plant a nuclear bomb inside an asteroid heading for Earth; Ben Affleck and Liv Tyler, and an Aerosmith song. Not Deep Impact.
Edward Norton as a former neo-Nazi skinhead who comes out of prison changed and tries to stop his younger brother (Edward Furlong) from following him; the flashbacks are in black and white.
Brendan Fraser as an adventurer who accidentally awakens the cursed Egyptian priest Imhotep at Hamunaptra, with Rachel Weisz as a librarian. The 1999 one, not the Tom Cruise reboot.
Kevin Spacey as a suburban dad in a midlife crisis who quits his job and obsesses over his daughter's friend; the plastic bag blowing in the wind and the rose petals.
Hugh Grant runs a travel bookshop in London and the biggest Hollywood star, Julia Roberts, walks in; he spills orange juice on her and they fall in love.
Tom Hanks as a FedEx systems engineer stranded on a desert island after a plane crash; his only companion is a football I think, named Wilson, and he knocks out his own tooth with an ice skate.
Julia Roberts as a single mother working at a law firm who uncovers that a power company poisoned a town's water with chromium; true story, Steven Soderbergh.
Denzel Washington as a corrupt LAPD narcotics detective, Alonzo Harris, showing rookie Ethan Hawke the streets in one day; 'King Kong ain't got nothing on me'.
Pixar: the monsters Sulley and Mike scare children through closet doors to power their city, until a little girl they call Boo gets into the monster world.
Russell Crowe as the mathematician John Nash, who has schizophrenia and imagines a roommate and a government code-breaking mission; Jennifer Connelly as his wife. Ron Howard.
George Clooney and Brad Pitt assemble eleven con men to rob three Las Vegas casinos owned by Andy Garcia on a boxing night; Julia Roberts is the ex-wife. Not the Sinatra one.
Jake Gyllenhaal as a troubled teenager who sleepwalks out of his house the night a jet engine crashes into his bedroom; a man in a creepy rabbit costume called Frank says the world ends in 28 days.
Tobey Maguire as Peter Parker, bitten by a genetically modified spider, fights the Green Goblin (Willem Dafoe); the upside-down kiss with Mary Jane in the rain. The Sam Raimi one.
Leonardo DiCaprio as teenage con artist Frank Abagnale who poses as a Pan Am pilot, a doctor and a lawyer and forges cheques while FBI agent Tom Hanks chases him. Spielberg, true story.
Matt Damon is pulled out of the sea with bullets in his back and no memory, only a Swiss bank account number in his hip, and he turns out to be a trained CIA assassin; a Mini Cooper chase in Paris.
Adrien Brody as Władysław Szpilman, a Jewish pianist who survives the Warsaw ghetto by hiding, helped at the end by a German officer. Roman Polanski.

film: The Lord of the Rings: The Return of the King
query: The last part: Frodo and Sam with Gollum climb Mount Doom to destroy the ring while Aragorn leads the armies at Minas Tirith; won eleven Oscars. Not the first one.
Uma Thurman as the Bride in a yellow tracksuit who wakes from a coma and takes revenge on the assassins who shot her at her wedding; the fight with the Crazy 88 and O-Ren Ishii in Tokyo. Tarantino.
Christmas in London with interlinked love stories: Hugh Grant as the Prime Minister, the cue cards on the doorstep, and Bill Nighy's old rocker singing 'Christmas Is All Around'.
Clint Eastwood directs: Sean Penn's daughter is murdered in Boston and his childhood friends, a detective played by Kevin Bacon and Tim Robbins, who was abducted as a boy, get pulled in.
An old man reads a love story from a notebook to a woman with dementia: Ryan Gosling's Noah and Rachel McAdams's Allie in the 1940s South; the kiss in the rain.
Pixar family of superheroes forced into hiding: Mr. Incredible is lured back by the villain Syndrome, with Elastigirl, Dash, Violet, baby Jack-Jack and the designer Edna Mode ('no capes').
Clint Eastwood as an old boxing trainer who reluctantly turns Hilary Swank's waitress into a champion; Morgan Freeman narrates, tragic ending.
Lindsay Lohan as a teen raised in Africa who starts at an American high school and infiltrates the Plastics led by Regina George; Tina Fey wrote it, 'on Wednesdays we wear pink'.
Christian Bale as Bruce Wayne trains with the League of Shadows under Ra's al Ghul and fights the Scarecrow's fear toxin in Gotham. The first of Nolan's trilogy, not The Dark Knight.
A masked anarchist in a Guy Fawkes mask (Hugo Weaving) fights a fascist British government and plans to blow up Parliament on the fifth of November; Natalie Portman has her head shaved.
Daniel Craig's first Bond: a high-stakes poker game in Montenegro against the terrorist banker Le Chiffre, who weeps blood; Vesper Lynd and the torture chair scene.
Will Smith as Chris Gardner, a struggling single father selling bone density scanners, who takes an unpaid stockbroker internship; he and his son sleep in a subway station bathroom. True story.
A dysfunctional family drives a yellow VW bus that has to be push-started to get the little daughter to a beauty pageant; Steve Carell as the suicidal uncle and Alan Arkin as the grandpa.
Clive Owen in a future Britain where no baby has been born for 18 years escorts the first pregnant woman in decades to safety; long single-shot scenes, Alfonso Cuarón.
Gerard Butler as King Leonidas leads 300 Spartans against the Persian army of Xerxes at Thermopylae, stylised slow motion, 'This is Sparta!'

Josh Brolin finds two million dollars at a drug deal gone wrong in Texas and is hunted by the killer Anton Chigurh (Javier Bardem) with a cattle gun and a coin toss; Tommy Lee Jones is the sheriff. Coen brothers.
Pixar: Remy, a rat in Paris who dreams of being a chef, controls a clumsy kitchen boy, Linguini, by pulling his hair; the food critic Anton Ego.
Daniel Day-Lewis as the oilman Daniel Plainview in early 1900s California, against a young preacher, Eli Sunday (Paul Dano); 'I drink your milkshake'.
Jonah Hill and Michael Cera as high school best friends trying to buy alcohol for a party with their nerdy friend's fake ID that says McLovin, who spends the night with two goofy cops.
Robert Downey Jr. as Tony Stark, a weapons billionaire kidnapped in Afghanistan, builds an armoured suit in a cave to escape; the first Marvel movie, 'I am Iron Man' at the end.
Pixar: a lonely trash-compacting robot left on an abandoned Earth falls in love with a sleek probe robot called EVE and follows her to a spaceship full of lazy humans.
Liam Neeson as a retired CIA agent whose daughter is kidnapped in Paris by human traffickers; the phone call 'I have a very particular set of skills'.
Pixar: grumpy old Carl ties thousands of balloons to his house to fly to South America with a boy scout, Russell, stuck on the porch; the sad opening about his wife Ellie and the talking dog Dug.
Tarantino WWII film: Brad Pitt's Jewish-American soldiers scalp Nazis while a cinema owner plans to burn Hitler in her theatre; Christoph Waltz as Colonel Hans Landa.

Three friends wake up in a trashed Las Vegas suite after a bachelor party with a tiger in the bathroom, a baby and the groom missing; Zach Galifianakis, Bradley Cooper and a Mike Tyson cameo. The first one, not the sequels.
Aliens nicknamed prawns live in a slum in Johannesburg, and a bureaucrat played by Sharlto Copley who is evicting them gets sprayed with alien fluid and starts turning into one; mockumentary style.
Leonardo DiCaprio as a US marshal investigating a missing patient at a hospital for the criminally insane on an island in 1954, with Mark Ruffalo; the twist about who he really is. Scorsese.
Andy is leaving for college and Woody, Buzz and the toys end up donated to Sunnyside daycare run by a pink strawberry-smelling bear, Lotso; the incinerator scene. Not the first one.
Colin Firth as King George VI with a stammer, treated by an unconventional Australian speech therapist (Geoffrey Rush) before the wartime radio speech.
Natalie Portman as a ballerina cast as both the white and the black swan in Swan Lake, losing her mind under the pressure and the rival dancer Mila Kunis. Darren Aronofsky.
DreamWorks: Hiccup, a weak Viking boy, befriends an injured Night Fury dragon he names Toothless and builds it a tail fin. The first one.
1960s Mississippi: a young white writer, Skeeter (Emma Stone), interviews Black maids like Aibileen and Minny (Viola Davis, Octavia Spencer) for a book; the chocolate pie.

film: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows – Part 2
query: The final Harry Potter: the Battle of Hogwarts, breaking out of Gringotts on a dragon, Snape's memories in the Pensieve and Harry facing Voldemort. The last part, not Philosopher's Stone.
Ryan Gosling as a quiet Hollywood stunt driver who moonlights as a getaway driver, wears a scorpion jacket and falls for his neighbour Carey Mulligan; the elevator scene and synth music.

Batman comes out of retirement after eight years to face Bane, who breaks his back and throws him in a pit prison while taking over Gotham with a nuclear bomb; Anne Hathaway as Catwoman. The third Nolan one.
Jamie Foxx as a freed slave who becomes a bounty hunter with a German dentist (Christoph Waltz) to rescue his wife from Leonardo DiCaprio's plantation, Candyland. Tarantino.
Jennifer Lawrence as Katniss Everdeen, who volunteers in place of her sister for a televised fight to the death between teenagers from twelve districts; the mockingjay pin. The first one.
Ben Affleck as a CIA agent who gets six American diplomats out of Tehran in 1979 by pretending they are a Canadian crew scouting a fake sci-fi film. True story.
Daniel Craig's Bond: a former MI6 agent played by Javier Bardem hunts M, and it ends at the old family estate in Scotland with the Aston Martin; Adele song. Not Spectre.
Sandra Bullock and maybe Matt Damon as astronauts left drifting in orbit after debris destroys their shuttle; she has to reach the Chinese space station alone. Alfonso Cuarón.
Leonardo DiCaprio as Jordan Belfort, a stockbroker who gets rich through fraud, drugs and wild parties; Jonah Hill as his partner and the quaalude crawl. Scorsese.

Disney: Princess Anna goes after her sister Elsa, whose ice powers trapped their kingdom in eternal winter, with the iceman Kristoff, his reindeer Sven and the snowman Olaf; 'Let It Go'. The first one.
Chiwetel Ejiofor as Solomon Northup, a free Black man from New York kidnapped and sold into slavery in Louisiana; Michael Fassbender as a cruel plantation owner. Steve McQueen.
Joaquin Phoenix as a lonely letter writer in near-future LA who falls in love with his computer's AI operating system, voiced by Scarlett Johansson. Spike Jonze.
Ben Affleck's wife Amy (Rosamund Pike) disappears on their anniversary and he becomes the suspect, but she has faked it to frame him. David Fincher.
Miles Teller as a young jazz drummer at a music conservatory, terrorised by the abusive bandleader Terence Fletcher (J. K. Simmons): 'not quite my tempo'.
Wes Anderson: the concierge Monsieur Gustave (Ralph Fiennes) and his lobby boy Zero get caught up in the theft of the painting 'Boy with Apple', in a pink hotel in a made-up European country.
Marvel: Star-Lord (Chris Pratt), a raccoon with guns, a tree that only says 'I am Groot', Gamora and Drax team up to protect an orb; a Walkman mixtape of 70s songs.
Benedict Cumberbatch as Alan Turing, who builds a machine to break the German Enigma code at Bletchley Park in WWII and is later prosecuted for being gay.
Tom Hardy as Max and Charlize Theron as Furiosa escape the warlord Immortan Joe across the desert in a war rig with his wives; the flame-throwing guitarist.
Matt Damon as an astronaut stranded on Mars after his crew think he is dead; he grows potatoes and has to science his way to survival until a rescue. Ridley Scott.
Pixar: the emotions Joy, Sadness, Anger, Fear and Disgust inside 11-year-old Riley's head after her family moves to San Francisco; Bing Bong the imaginary friend. The first one, not the sequel.
Leonardo DiCaprio as frontiersman Hugh Glass, mauled by a bear and left for dead by Tom Hardy's character in the 1820s, crawls back for revenge for his son; the role that finally won him the Oscar.
Boston Globe reporters (Michael Keaton, Mark Ruffalo, Rachel McAdams) investigate how the Catholic Church covered up child abuse by priests; won best picture.
Amy Adams as a linguist trying to talk to seven-limbed aliens who write in circular ink symbols after twelve shells land around the world; the twist about her daughter. Denis Villeneuve.
Disney: Judy Hopps becomes the first bunny police officer in a city of animals and teams up with the con artist fox Nick Wilde to find missing predators; the sloth at the DMV.
Andrew Garfield as Desmond Doss, a conscientious objector who refuses to carry a rifle and saves 75 men as an army medic at Okinawa. Mel Gibson directed.
Three chapters in the life of Chiron, a Black boy growing up in Miami, with a drug dealer father figure played by Mahershala Ali; won best picture after the envelope mix-up.
Christopher Nolan's WWII film about the evacuation of British soldiers from the beaches of Dunkirk, told on land, sea and air on three time scales; Harry Styles, and Tom Hardy as a Spitfire pilot.
Pixar: Miguel, a Mexican boy who wants to be a musician despite his family's ban, ends up in the Land of the Dead on Día de los Muertos and meets his ancestors; 'Remember Me'.
Frances McDormand as a mother who rents three billboards to call out the police chief (Woody Harrelson) for not solving her daughter's murder; Sam Rockwell as the racist cop.
A family survives in silence on a farm because blind monsters hunt by sound; Emily Blunt gives birth in a bathtub, and John Krasinski directed and plays the father. The first one.
Thanos (Josh Brolin) collects all six Infinity Stones and snaps his fingers to wipe out half of all life, after a big battle in Wakanda. Not Endgame, the one before it.
Rami Malek as Freddie Mercury in the Queen biopic, from forming the band to the Live Aid concert at Wembley.
Chadwick Boseman as T'Challa, king of the hidden African nation Wakanda, challenged by his cousin Killmonger (Michael B. Jordan); vibranium and the Dora Milaje. Marvel.

Animated: Brooklyn teen Miles Morales becomes Spider-Man and meets spider-people from other dimensions, an older Peter B. Parker, Spider-Gwen and Spider-Ham, against Kingpin's collider. The first one.
Viggo Mortensen as an Italian-American bouncer who drives the Black pianist Dr. Don Shirley (Mahershala Ali) on a concert tour of the Deep South in the 1960s; the fried chicken scene.
Rian Johnson whodunit: a rich crime novelist dies after his 85th birthday party, Daniel Craig is detective Benoit Blanc, and the nurse Marta throws up whenever she lies. Not Glass Onion.
Sam Mendes WWI film: two young British soldiers must cross no man's land to deliver a message calling off an attack that would kill 1,600 men, made to look like one continuous shot.

film: Once Upon a Time in Hollywood
query: Tarantino: a fading TV western actor (Leonardo DiCaprio) and his stunt double (Brad Pitt) in 1969 Los Angeles, next door to Sharon Tate, with an alternate ending to the Manson murders.

Christopher Nolan: John David Washington as the Protagonist, who learns to move through time inversion to stop a Russian oligarch from ending the world; a plane crashed into a hangar and a reverse car chase.
Pixar: Joe Gardner, a middle school music teacher who dreams of jazz, falls into a manhole just before his big gig, and his soul ends up mentoring 22, a soul who doesn't want to be born.
Frances McDormand as a widow who loses everything in the recession and lives in her van, travelling the American West and working seasonal jobs at an Amazon warehouse. Chloé Zhao.
Timothée Chalamet as Paul Atreides on the desert planet Arrakis with giant sandworms and the spice, betrayed by the Harkonnens. Denis Villeneuve's part one, not the 1984 version.
Tom Holland's Peter Parker asks Doctor Strange to make the world forget he is Spider-Man; the spell goes wrong, villains from other universes arrive and the older Spider-Men come back.
Ruby, the only hearing member of a deaf fishing family in Massachusetts, wants to sing and audition for Berklee instead of working on the boat; remake of a French film, won best picture.
Michelle Yeoh as a Chinese-American laundromat owner being audited by the IRS who jumps between universes, including one where people have hot dog fingers, to fight an evil version of her daughter.
Jake Sully and Neytiri's family flee to the reef people of Pandora and learn to ride sea creatures while Colonel Quaritch returns as an avatar; the outcast tulkun Payakan. The sequel.
Robert Pattinson as a young brooding Batman investigating a serial killer, the Riddler, who leaves puzzles for him in Gotham; Zoë Kravitz as Catwoman. Not the Christian Bale ones.

On an Irish island in 1923, Colin Farrell's simple farmer is devastated when his best friend (Brendan Gleeson) suddenly stops speaking to him and threatens to cut off his own fingers; the donkey Jenny.
Margot Robbie as Barbie, who leaves pink Barbieland for the real world with Ken (Ryan Gosling), who discovers patriarchy; Greta Gerwig, 'I'm Just Ken'.
Scorsese: the Osage murders in 1920s Oklahoma; Leonardo DiCaprio marries an Osage woman, Mollie, for her oil money while his uncle Robert De Niro plots to kill her family.
Animated sequel: Miles Morales follows Gwen into the Spider-Society led by Miguel O'Hara, the villain is The Spot, and it ends on a cliffhanger. Not the first one.
Emma Stone as Bella Baxter, a woman revived by a scientist (Willem Dafoe) with the brain of her unborn baby, who runs off on an adventure across Europe with a lawyer (Mark Ruffalo). Yorgos Lanthimos.
A grumpy classics teacher (Paul Giamatti) at a New England boarding school has to look after the students who can't go home over Christmas in 1970, with a grieving cook. Alexander Payne.
Paul Atreides joins the Fremen with Chani (Zendaya), rides a giant sandworm and leads a holy war against the Harkonnens, with Austin Butler as Feyd-Rautha. The second part.
Pixar sequel: Riley turns 13 and new emotions Anxiety, Envy, Ennui and Embarrassment take over headquarters during a hockey camp. The sequel, not the first one.
Ryan Reynolds as Deadpool teams up with a broken variant of Wolverine (Hugh Jackman) in the Void to save his timeline from the TVA; lots of cameos.
Movie musical: green-skinned Elphaba (Cynthia Erivo) and popular Glinda (Ariana Grande) become friends at Shiz University before Elphaba turns against the Wizard of Oz; 'Defying Gravity'. Part one.
Sean Baker film: Ani, a young stripper from Brooklyn, marries the son of a Russian oligarch in Las Vegas and his family's henchmen come to get it annulled; won best picture.
Demi Moore as an ageing fitness TV star who uses a black-market drug that creates a younger version of herself (Margaret Qualley), and they must switch every seven days; body horror.
Ralph Fiennes as a cardinal running the secret vote to elect a new pope in the Vatican after the pope dies, uncovering scandals about the candidates; a twist at the end.
Michael B. Jordan plays twin brothers who open a juke joint in 1930s Mississippi, and vampires drawn by their young cousin's blues guitar lay siege to it. Ryan Coogler.
James Gunn's reboot with David Corenswet as Superman and his dog Krypto; Lex Luthor turns the public against him after he stops an invasion. Not Man of Steel.
Brad Pitt as an ageing former Formula One driver who comes back to help a struggling team and mentor a hotshot rookie; Joseph Kosinski, with Lewis Hamilton as a producer.
Paul Thomas Anderson: Leonardo DiCaprio as a burned-out ex-revolutionary who has to rescue his daughter when an old enemy, a military officer played by Sean Penn, comes after them.
Ryan Gosling as a school science teacher who wakes up alone on a spaceship with amnesia, sent to save the Sun, and befriends a spider-like alien he calls Rocky. Based on the Andy Weir novel.
